statement: For iid bond percolation on the infinite path Z, p_c=1 and theta(p_c)=1, so the p_c<1 hypothesis in the quasi-transitive criticality conjecture is necessary.
proof_or_counterexample: For p<1 an infinite component at 0 requires every edge of one infinite ray open, probability at most 2 lim_n p^n=0; at p=1 the entire Z graph is open.
remaining_gap: None for the boundary example; it does not prove critical nonpercolation when p_c<1.

statement: For a countable graph G and p>0, almost surely every infinite component C of Bernoulli-p(G) has p_c(C)>=min(1,p_c(G)/p).
assumptions: p_c defined by positive probability of any infinite cluster
proof_or_counterexample: For every rational q with pq<p_c(G), the products of original p-bits and fresh q-bits are iid Bernoulli-pq and have no infinite component almost surely. Tonelli conditions on the original configuration; its countably many open components each fail q-percolation with conditional probability one. Intersect the rational-q probability-one events and use monotonicity.
remaining_gap: Critical infinite clusters have intrinsic p_c=1; this necessary fragility does not rule them out.

statement: For fixed p>p_c on a bounded-degree countable graph with 0<p_c<1, each infinite Bernoulli-p component C satisfies h(C,o)<=log(Delta^2+1)/log(p/(p-p_c)) for every o in C, where h is the infimum of H-edge boundary divided by size over finite rooted connected vertex sets.
assumptions: h defined by all finite rooted connected sets
proof_or_counterexample: The rooted connected-set counting bound gives p_c(C)<=1-(Delta^2+1)^(-1/h) when h>0; quenched thinning gives p_c(C)>=p_c/p. Rearranging yields the bound; h=0 is immediate.
remaining_gap: Requires L004 to state q in [0,1); only a necessary expansion bound, not a proof of P0043.

statement: The decorated-ray graph in w441-L005 has exponential volume growth but p_c=1; its published proof text needs a uniform-radius argument to justify liminf growth.
assumptions: finite binary tree of depth n attached at s_n
proof_or_counterexample: For every radius r>=1 take n=floor((r-1)/2); its 2^n leaves are within distance 2n+1<=r of s_0, so liminf |B(s_0,r)|^(1/r)>=sqrt(2). Every infinite path must use arbitrarily long spine segments, each open with probability q^m->0 for q<1.
remaining_gap: Add this radius interpolation and a graph-invariant orbit argument to the peer artifact before promotion.
